Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statement :**

All Bananas are Grapes.

All Papayas are Pineapple.

Some Pineapples are Banana.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some Papayas are Grapes.

(II) Some Grapes are Pineapples.

(III) Some Bananas are Papayas.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and III follow
Both Conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
From the given statements, we draw a Venn diagram:

All Bananas are Grapes.

All Papayas are Pineapple.

(II) Some Grapes are Pineapples **→ Follow → **As all bananas are grapes and some pineapples are bananas so it can be also said that some grapes are pineapples and therefore the conclusion follows.

Since **only conclusion II follows.**

Hence **the correct answer is option 2)**

questions.question: Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 76 has provided for the office of the AGI.
 
• Appointed by **President.**__
 
• AGI must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• AGI must be a citizen of India and he must have been a judge of some high court for 5 years or an advocate of some high court for 10 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The **power **of Attorney General is **he gives advice to the government of India **upon such legal matters, which are referred or assigned to him by the President and he represents such other duties of a legal character that are referred or assigned to him by** the President.**
 
• **Impeachment:- **Procedures and grounds for the removal of** AGI** are not stated in the Constitution. She/he holds office during the contentment of the President.
 
 
• AGI may be removed by the** President** at **any time**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pair of co-primes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Two numbers are co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1.

→ (31, 93) has an HCF of 31, and (14, 35) has an HCF of 7.

→ (32, 62) are both even numbers, meaning their HCF is at least 2.

→ (25, 31) has an HCF of 1 because 31 is a prime number and not a factor of 25.

**∴ The correct answer is the pair (25, 31).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Concept Used:**

Two numbers are said to be co-prime (or relatively prime) if they share no common factors other than 1. Their HCF must be equal to 1.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us find the factors for the numbers in each given pair.

⇒ For pair (31, 93): Factors of 31 are 1, 31. Factors of 93 are 1, 3, 31, 93. Since the highest common factor is 31, they are not co-prime.

⇒ For pair (32, 62): Both numbers are even, meaning they are perfectly divisible by 2. Thus, they are not co-prime.

⇒ For pair (14, 35): 14 = 2 × 7 and 35 = 5 × 7. Since the highest common factor is 7, they are not co-prime.

⇒ For pair (25, 31): 25 = 5 × 5 and 31 is a prime number. The only common factor between them is 1.

⇒ Because the highest common factor of 25 and 31 is exactly 1, they are co-primes.

**∴ The correct answer is the pair (25, 31).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct factors: 1 and itself. Example: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.

Twin Primes

A pair of prime numbers that have a difference of exactly 2. Example: (3, 5), (5, 7), (11, 13).

Properties of Co-primes

Co-prime numbers do not have to be prime themselves (e.g., 8 and 15 are co-prime). Furthermore, the LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.
